root_cause: Segment._split_cells guesses a starting index proportionally, pos = int(cut/cell_length*len(text)) - 1, then only scans FORWARD. When wide (CJK) characters sit before narrow ones (e.g. trailing spaces, as in 'メルク (CV: 水瀬いのり)     '), the guess already overshoots: cell_len(text[:pos]) > cut. The forward loop never backtracks, so it returns a left segment wider than cut (reproduced locally: cut=21 starts at pos 14 with 22 cells and returns a 23-cell left). The hidden test failure was the same kind of error: 'assert 24 == 23'.
best_solution: Rewrite the search in rich/segment.py::Segment._split_cells as a loop that can move both ways: start at pos = int(cut/cell_length*len(text)); in `while True` compute before=text[:pos], out_by = cell_len(before) - cut; if out_by == 0 return (before, text[pos:]); if out_by == -1 and text[pos] is double-width, split that character into two spaces: (text[:pos]+' ', ' '+text[pos+1:]); if out_by == +1 and text[pos-1] is double-width, return (text[:pos-1]+' ', ' '+text[pos:]); otherwise pos += 1 if cell_pos < cut else pos -= 1. Keep the existing early return for cut >= cell_length. The reasoning from the statement alone: 'split_cells fix' plus the existing test_split_cells_mixed (which already cites a Textual CJK issue) points to this function. Checking the invariant cell_len(left) == cut for every cut from 0 to cell_length on mixed CJK/ASCII strings exposes the one-way scan after an overshooting guess.
acceptable_alternatives: Any split that makes cell_len(left)==cut and cell_len(right)==total-cut for every cut passes. The simplest is our v6 patch: start at pos=0, cell_pos=0 and keep the forward scan (O(n), always correct). Another option is to clamp the guess by stepping pos back while cell_len(text[:pos]) > cut and then running the old forward loop.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_segment.py::test_split_cells_mixed is parametrized over 8 CJK/ASCII strings: '早乙女リリエル (CV: 徳井青）', 'メイド・イン・きゅんクチュアリ☆    ', 'TVアニメ「メルクストーリア -無気力少年と瓶の中の少女-」 主題歌CD', '南無阿弥JKうらめしや?！     ', and 'メルク (CV: 水瀬いのり)     ' with 0 to 2 leading spaces and 5 or 6 trailing spaces. For EVERY position in range(0, cell_length+1), Segment.split_cells(segment, position) must give cell_len(left.text) == position and cell_len(right.text) == cell_length - position. Position 0 and the full length are included. A wide character cut in half becomes two spaces, one on each side.
locating_signals: The title names the method outright: 'Segment.split_cells fix' leads to rich/segment.py Segment.split_cells, which delegates to _split_cells. The only other content is a link to Textual issue #5090. The existing test_split_cells_mixed already mentions a Textual CJK issue (#4996), which shows the bug class is mixed-width text. The statement never says what is wrong (the proportional start guess overshooting), so the agent has to find the defect by fuzzing positions.
our_outcome_summary: Only v6 passed. v6 (34s, 12 calls) replaced the proportional guess with pos=0, before='', cell_pos=0, so the forward-only scan can never start past cut. That is correct, just slower than gold. v4 (91s, 27 calls) failed: it kept the overshooting start and only changed the padding in the cell_pos > cut branch to ' ' * split_before / split_after, which does nothing about the actual defect. v7 (42s, 14 calls) produced an empty patch. v8 (62s, 29 calls) was a cosmetic refactor (inlined `before` into text[:pos]) with no change in behavior. v4, v7 and v8 all failed the same 4 of 8 params (segment1/3/4/7, all strings ending in narrow characters) with errors like 'assert 24 == 23'.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is only a title plus an external link ('X.method fix'), write a quick property check of the method's invariant over its whole input range (here: for every cut in 0..len, width(left)==cut and width(right)==total-cut) on adversarial inputs (wide characters first, narrow at the end, leading/trailing spaces). Then fix the search logic that breaks it. Be suspicious of heuristic 'estimate then scan one direction' loops: the estimate can overshoot, so make the scan bidirectional or start from a known-safe point. Patches that only touch the output formatting of the branch that happens to fire, or that refactor without changing behavior, rarely fix these bugs.
